<issue>
OAuth2 error handling broken when catch_errors is True

#### Description

When `catch_errors` is set to `True` on OAuth2 endpoints, exceptions are not being properly caught and handled. Instead of returning appropriate error responses, the exceptions are being raised directly, causing server errors.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from oauthlib.oauth2 import Server, RequestValidator

# Create a server with error catching enabled
validator = RequestValidator()
server = Server(validator)
server.catch_errors = True

# This should return a server_error response but raises an exception instead
h, b, s = server.create_token_response('https://example.com', body='grant_type=authorization_code&code=abc')
print(f"Status: {s}, Body: {b}")  # Expected: Status 500 with server_error in body
```

The issue affects all OAuth2 endpoint types (web, mobile, legacy, backend) when `catch_errors=True`. Instead of gracefully handling exceptions and returning proper error responses with status code 500, the exceptions are being raised directly.
</issue>
